X.note: The 3D block tower is a good visual metaphor, and the main label (1,849 Mt, ACTUAL) is large and clear. The tower is cropped at the top. The 1950 and U.S. 81.9 Mt labels are dim grey on dark and weak on a phone. The 1950 block is tiny and its connection to the data is unclear. The orange U.S. sliver is hard to see. The source text is small. The gridlines run behind the tower and don't line up with the blocks, so the scale is hard to check. The 1,500/1,000/500 labels don't obviously match the 100 Mt blocks. The 1950 value is never stated.

Y.note: This is a clean two-bar chart with large text and strong contrast, and the point reads in about 2 seconds: 72% to 77%, still short of the 80% benchmark. The dashed 80% line runs through the '≈ 72%' and '≈ 77%' labels, which hurts readability. The 80% label sits slightly off the line. The bars have no axis, so the lengths are not clearly proportional (80% falls only a little past the 77% bar). The blurred background is a dull placeholder. The source line is smaller but legible.

why: Y delivers one clear message with large, high-contrast text that holds up on a phone, while X's nicer 3D concept is undercut by cropping, dim secondary labels and an unclear scale.
top_fix_for_weaker: In X, pull the camera back so the tower's top and the 1,849 Mt callout are fully in frame. Make the 1950 and U.S. 81.9 Mt labels bright white at about 1.5x size. Print the 1950 value on its label. Stretch the 1950 block taller and brighten the orange U.S. portion so the 4% share is visible. Enlarge the source text or shorten it.
